reading.body:
DartPoints Shreveport operates 2.2 MW of published IT capacity in downtown Shreveport, translating to roughly 55 racks at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack.

The facility is one of three data centers for which DartPoints acquired underlying real estate in April 2025, when NOVA Infrastructure took majority control of the operator with over 250 million dollars in committed growth capital. DartPoints runs 11 facilities across 10 regional markets in tier-2 and tier-3 United States metros, serving more than 900 enterprise customers. The company markets itself on AI-ready, high-density infrastructure with 99.999 percent uptime and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This Shreveport node is the third largest by published capacity in Louisiana, accounting for one of 7.7 MW across the four facilities mapped in the state.

The facility represents the regional colocation tier rather than hyperscaler infrastructure. It offers fixed capacity to enterprise tenants, universities, and hospital systems rather than operating as an AI-native platform. At 2.2 MW, it sits well outside the scale that shapes national AI compute constraints, though it may serve local enterprise and university demand for managed infrastructure.

The data published does not cover local power availability, grid constraints, planned capacity expansion, or utilization rates at this address. DartPoints' strategy targets communities outside major metros, but whether Shreveport's grid can support significant expansion remains undocumented.
